name: Maximum Red Purple
lede: Maximum Red Purple is a deep magenta from Crayola's "Maximum" crayon line, a 1990s set built to give the most saturated version of each mixed hue its own name.

sections.title: A maximum of red and purple
sections.body:
Crayola's "Maximum" crayons, including Maximum Red Purple, Maximum Blue Purple and Maximum Green Yellow, name a color by its two parent hues and claim the fullest saturation of that mix [1]. Our library carries this one from Wikipedia's color lists, with no further paper trail, so who coined the exact name and when is undocumented in the sources checked here [1].

Its nearest named neighbors by measured color are [[magenta-haze]] and [[mystic-maroon]], almost the same color but a touch brighter, with [[fandango]] and [[amaranth-deep-purple]] close behind [1]. The hex value is a screen approximation; no pigment or dye sits behind it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 79 percent of the named colors we track [2]. Every one of the three uses it as an accent, not a dominant color [2]. The small count may reflect how uncommon the exact mix is in paint, or how thin our coverage is for this hue; a color match here is not a pigment identification [2].
